Isolated W4A16 fused GEMV implementation and accuracy check
Memory summary

With baseline latency established, the agent implemented a standalone Triton W4A16 GEMV to validate fused int4 unpacking and dequantization before integrating it into the full decode block. The kernel passed six shape checks with cosine similarity from 0.999997 to 0.999998; the highlighted case, K=2304, N=4096, had cosine 0.999998.

Relevant prior context

Important non-obvious context

The task’s packed weights store adjacent input rows in the low and high nibbles of each uint8. Each group of 128 input elements has bf16 scales and zeros per output. The new kernel computes the affine dequantized dot product by accumulating nibble-weighted activations and subtracting the zero-point contribution, without materializing a bf16 weight matrix.

This unit validates the GEMV in isolation; it does not yet implement the full model forward or meet the task’s single-launch full-step requirement. The trace’s file path names a 03_kimi_linear_decode directory even though this run is for problem 02_kimi_linear_decode.

Recording summary

The agent began this unit by noting the baseline range and choosing to build and unit-test the core W4A16 GEMV. It wrote k_gemv.py with a Triton kernel that assigns each program a tile of output columns, loops over input groups, loads even and odd activations, extracts the low and high nibbles, and accumulates the affine dequantized result. A small Python reference packer, quantizer, unpacker, and dequantizer were included for testing; no reference module was imported.

The kernel’s group contribution is equivalent to scale * (sum(x_even * low_nibble + x_odd * high_nibble) - zero * sum(x)). It stores the accumulated result as bf16. The test used six (K, N) shapes, including the main projection size (2304, 4096).
